description: Source-checked public opportunity statements; NOT proof of approval, individual eligibility, settled revenue, or current service availability.

opportunities.claim: Cloudflare announced October 30 that beginning November 4, 2026, D1 queries returning more than 50 MB will fail. REST API import and export operations are exempt. Cloudflare says the limit covers the 99.999th percentile of D1 queries.
opportunities.eligibility: Existing or future Cloudflare D1 users whose SQL queries return more than 50 MB; no proof that this founder currently uses D1.
opportunities.friction: Requires identifying oversized result sets, selecting needed columns and paginating. No new account, fee, or migration requirement announced.
opportunities.title: Cloudflare D1 50 MB query result ceiling effective November 4
opportunities.value: Avoid oversized-query failures; no direct cash, credits, or revenue. Pagination and narrow column selection may prevent errors.
opportunities.why_now: Newly announced dated operational constraint. Relevant to developers producing large data feeds or analytics exports; LEVERAGE//SEEKER has no verified active D1 deployment, so no immediate owner task.

opportunities.claim: As of October 30 Browser Run defaults to Chrome 152. Quick Actions default User-Agent changed from Chrome 119 to Chrome 152, /links returns absolute URLs, links-only crawls follow relative links, and Markdown output retains code block languages.
opportunities.eligibility: Browser Run is offered on Cloudflare Workers Free and Paid. Published Free allowance: 10 browser minutes/day; plan and account access unverified.
opportunities.friction: Free quota is limited; paid usage and concurrent browser fees apply beyond included Paid plan allowances. Browser scraping must respect site policies and copyright. Pricing: https://developers.cloudflare.com/browser-run/pricing/
opportunities.title: Cloudflare Browser Run Chrome 152 and improved source extraction
opportunities.value: Potentially fewer failed page reads and more reliable link normalization; not quantified and not customer revenue.
opportunities.why_now: New release improves link provenance and extraction quality for source-verified research, but any automation matching the old User-Agent may require review. No evidence the current LEVERAGE//SEEKER repository uses Browser Run.

opportunities.claim: GitHub announced GA on 2026-10-28 for Free, Team and Enterprise plans. The gh actions-lock extension can lock workflow actions, transitive dependencies and reusable workflows to exact commits; Dependabot can refresh lockfiles.
opportunities.eligibility: GitHub Actions repositories on Free, Team or Enterprise; CLI extension setup and per-workflow onboarding required.
opportunities.friction: Install and review gh actions-lock; commit generated lockfile; review dependencies for trustworthiness. No first-customer impact.
opportunities.title: GitHub Actions workflow dependency lockfiles generally available
opportunities.value: No separate license requirement announced for GitHub Free; potential avoided supply-chain incidents, not measurable revenue.
opportunities.why_now: Newly available stable dependency pinning is relevant to the public evidence repository, whose CI references version tags. This reduces unplanned dependency drift, not the need to review code.

opportunities.claim: Applications are open through 2026-11-20 for an early-stage cybersecurity incubator. The 12-week cohort has 10 company places, covers India/GCC/US, and offers up to $5,000 in KeyVigil model-gateway credits, mentorship and partner access.
opportunities.eligibility: Pre-seed/seed cybersecurity founders; idea-stage accepted with strong team and clearly defined security problem. U.S. among stated markets; individual fit and admission not established.
opportunities.friction: 12-week commitment, only 10 companies, selection process; no public application fee stated; requires cybersecurity product fit.
opportunities.title: CloudSEK Launchpad cybersecurity incubator cohort 1
opportunities.value: Up to $5,000 in KeyVigil credits for selected cohort companies; not cash, not guaranteed, not a general-purpose cloud grant.
opportunities.why_now: Newly surfaced active deadline and attractive advertised credit amount; rejected for the present LEVERAGE//SEEKER/SECONDS MATTER scope because the program explicitly targets cybersecurity founders, not general opportunity intelligence or home-service automation.
